title: W7: the work between team agents recorded for training, each task's owning team as a decision, team rename and removal, and the owner's acceptance checks end to end
request: Continue the collaborative workspace from the handover's 'Left to do': the W6 open items, then W7 (capture and acceptance).
plan: W6 follow-ups: team memory routes, a retry route for a failed correction fix-up, steady timing tests.
dclab-core 0.166.0: experience v18 with the team.task.*, team.action.*, team.report.* and team membership kinds; the ledger point team.task_owner.
Emit them where the work is saved; rename and remove teams (owner only).
The owner's seven acceptance checks as one end-to-end test on files and PostgreSQL.

decisions.decision: Events carry ids, names, states and counts only; a report's answer as agent text
decisions.why: never a cell, a team's private note or a team's name (the name stays in the audit trail)

decisions.decision: A top-level task's owning team is recorded as the asking team's agent's rule, not the person's choice
decisions.why: the deterministic agent picks the team; the initiator is only the member the work acts for

decisions.decision: A team with open work cannot be removed
decisions.why: its replies would land in a thread no member can read any more

change: dclab_core experience.py, ledger.py, workflow_labels.py, adapters; dclab_rnd teamspace/store.py, ledger/capture.py and __init__.py, store/tasks.py, storage/teams.py, agentic/routers/teams.py and memory.py, api_models.py, accounts/guard.py; tests/test_team_acceptance.py and others; CORE_INTEGRATION.md.

findings.defect: The delivery timing tests failed on a busy machine
findings.scenario: another session's gate loaded the machine: the backoff read -0.16 s and the cut-off 0.93 s
findings.cause: the wait was measured from the reader's clock after the call
findings.fix: a failed attempt records failed_at and the wait is measured from it; the cut-off has a wide margin

findings.defect: A team's memory had no route and a failed correction fix-up had no retry
findings.scenario: team_work.error was shown with no way to finish the work
findings.cause: W6 built the functions but not the routes
findings.fix: GET/POST team memory routes, members only; POST memory/base/reconcile, idempotent

findings.defect: The acceptance file re-ran every walkthrough test it imported
findings.scenario: importing the W5 contract brought its test methods into the new classes
findings.fix: the inherited tests are set to None in the acceptance base

findings.defect: Every routing decision was refused by the ledger, so nothing was recorded
findings.scenario: team_task_routed printed 'from_team: not a state field' and returned None
findings.cause: the state keys were not in STATE_FIELDS, and the tests patched the recorder and had no ledger
findings.fix: the fields are allowed (child as a flag); the acceptance tests use a real ledger and read the stored record

findings.scenario: it read a project that was never created
findings.fix: a second project with its own problem and task; each project's deliveries, threads and history never show the other's

findings.scenario: only the action's directory binding was asserted
findings.cause: the evidence was never tied to the task's allowed inputs
findings.fix: every shared evidence source is one of the task's allowed inputs

findings.defect: Removing a team with open work stranded its threads
findings.scenario: delete Business while T-renewal is open, make it again: the reply lands in a thread no member reads
findings.fix: 409 while the team owns or asked for an open task

outcome: The owner's seven acceptance checks pass end to end on files and PostgreSQL, with every task, action and report recorded as an event and each task's owning team stored as a ledger decision.
lessons: A test that patches the recorder can hide that the real recorder refuses every row: read what was stored.
risks: When a model writes reports (R4), a report's answer becomes model text; an output reference may carry real values once R3 reads real tables.
